meta_hook: See how direct lender referrals speed up business-purpose funding decisions.
takeaway: Commercial property loans in Brisbane fund business-purpose transactions, established asset purchases and construction or development projects, secured by land or property. Rather than routing every enquiry through a generic broker funnel, a direct referral pathway like Lender Direct sends the deal to lenders matched by security type, loan amount, purpose and exit, and only those with genuine appetite make contact. It excludes consumer credit, personal loans and owner-occupied home lending entirely.
lead_tail: in Brisbane follow a different assessment path to a standard home loan, and getting the security and exit structured correctly from the outset often decides whether a lender looks twice.

sections.h2: What counts as a commercial property loan
sections.html:
A commercial property loan is business-purpose finance secured against land, an established building, or a development site, rather than a home someone intends to live in. Lenders assess the deal on the security and the exit, not on the borrower's payslip. Lender Direct operates as a referral service that puts a funding request in front of lenders active in this space, rather than pushing it through a generic consumer finance funnel.

The distinction matters in Brisbane's commercial market because the paperwork, timing and risk appetite for an established asset purchase differ from those for a construction or development loan. Getting the enquiry in front of the right type of lender the first time avoids wasted back and forth.

Full detail on how enquiries are routed is on the Lender Direct site.

sections.h2: Two funding paths: buying versus building
sections.html:
Two broad paths cover most enquiries: buying land or an already-built asset, or funding the construction or development of one. Each carries a different risk profile for a lender.

  • Established asset purchase: security already exists and is income-producing or occupiable, which typically gives a lender a clearer read on value.
  • Construction or development: security is being created, so a lender wants clarity on the build program, the exit, and the transaction profile before deciding whether the deal fits.

Neither path is inherently better; it comes down to matching the security and exit to a lender genuinely active in that space, which is the reason the enquiry is routed rather than broadcast.

The process runs in three steps: the enquiry is routed by security type, purpose, loan amount, exit and transaction profile, not treated as a generic application. Where a lender in the network has genuine appetite for the deal, they contact you directly, which keeps the conversation closer to the decision-maker. If the opportunity isn't a fit for the lenders available, you're told as soon as practical, rather than left waiting.

Submitting enough detail at the outset, security, loan amount, exit strategy and the key numbers behind the deal, gives a lender a real basis to decide whether to look closer. You can see the funding enquiry form for the specifics.

sections.h2: What to prepare before you enquire
sections.html:
Because this is business-purpose lending assessed on the deal rather than a personal income test, having the following ready speeds up a lender's read:

  • The security: an established, income-producing asset, or a site to be developed or constructed.
  • The loan amount and how it fits against the value of the security.
  • The exit strategy, sale, refinance, or lease-up, since this is central to how a private lender assesses risk.
  • Contact details so an interested lender can reach you directly.

For construction deals, lenders generally want a clear build program and confirmation of how the loan gets repaid once the project completes, whether by sale, refinance, or lease income, before they commit funds in stages. None of this is assessed against a payslip or personal serviceability test the way a standard home loan is, since it's the deal itself under review. General guidance on how loan-to-value ratio and serviceability are typically assessed is available through ASIC Moneysmart.

This is built for business-purpose transactions: buying an established commercial asset, or funding construction or development, secured by the property itself. It is not designed for owner-occupied home loans, personal or consumer credit, or principal-place-of-residence funding, and enquiries outside that scope aren't a fit.

If you're weighing a commercial purchase or development against a standard home loan, a licensed mortgage broker or adviser can help clarify which pathway actually applies before you approach any lender.

faq.q: What is a commercial property loan?
faq.a: Business-purpose finance secured by land, an established building, or a development site, used to buy or build a commercial asset rather than a home to live in.

faq.q: Does this cover owner-occupied or residential home loans?
faq.a: No. This referral pathway is limited to commercial and business-purpose lending; owner-occupied home loans, personal loans and consumer credit fall outside it.

faq.q: How does the direct referral model differ from a standard broker?
faq.a: The enquiry is routed to lenders matched on security, purpose and exit, and an interested lender contacts you directly rather than through a broker intermediary.

faq.q: What happens if no lender in the network is interested?
faq.a: You're told as soon as practical that the opportunity isn't a fit for the lenders available, rather than left without a response.

faq.q: What information should I have ready before enquiring?
faq.a: The security type, loan amount, exit strategy and contact details, so a lender can form a genuine view quickly.
